# Method of approach

## System Overview
- Self Hosted Github Actions runner integrated with physical Raspberry Pi pIco hardware

- Enables automated execution of code on real embedded hardware

- System bridges GitHubs CI infrastructure with a hardware execution layer

- communicates via USB/ serial interface

## Hardware-in-the-Loop Architecture
- Implements hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing model which compiled firmware is automatically deployed to physical hardware for execution and validation

- Separates code compilation from execution while preserving automated feedback

- Ensures deterministic hardware behavior that more accurately reflects real deployment conditions

- supports repeatable experiments by resetting the device between runs

- Enables observation of hardware specific behaviors such as timing and deployment failures

### Hardware Components
- Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040 microcontroller)
  - Dual core ARM Cortex-M0+ microcontroller used as the execution target
  - chosen for low cost availability and strong open source tooling support.
  - commonly used in embedded systems courses and projects 

- Host machine running Docker
  - Serves as self-hosted GitHub Actions runner
  - manages container execution, device flashing and result collection
  - bridges gap between GitHubs CI infrastructure and physical hardware

- USB interface for flashing and serial communication

  - Used for firmware flashing via UF2 or OpenOCD based workflows
  - provides serial communication for runtime output and status reporting


### Software Components

- GitHub Actions
  - Orchestrates CI workflow including code checkout, build, deployment to hardware, and result collection
  - Provides extensible platform for integrating custom actions and scripts

- Self Hosted runner
    - executions GitHub Actions jobs locally on the host machine
    - allows direct access to connected hardware devices which is not possible with GitHub hosted runners
  
  - Docker
    - Used to containerize the build and deployment environment

    - consistent toolchains and dependencies across runs

    - provides isolation between student code and the host system

  - flashing and debugging tools
    - OpenOCD, and PIco SDK tools used for firmware deployment

  - Serial monitoring utilities
   - capture runtime output from the microcontroller
   forward execution results back to the CI pipeline


## Continuous Integration Workflow

- Workflow triggered by repository events such as push or pull request

- compiled firmware is deployed to the Raspberry Pi Pico over USB

- The device executes the program on real hardware

- Serial output and execution status are captured an logged

- results are reported back to GitHub actions for pass/fail evaluation

- workflow supports automated grading and validation without manual intervention

## Containerization and Isolation Strategy

- Each job runs inside a DOcker container wit predefine toolchain 

- containers prevent student code form directly accessing the host operating system

- hardware access is restricted to explicitly mounted USB devices

- Containers are destroyed after each run prevent state persistent 

- Isolation reduces risk fo cross submission interference

- Ensures readability of builds and executions across runs


## Security and Access Control

- Only trusted repositories are allowed to trigger hardware execution workflows

- To be able to access the self hosted runner you must have a repository inside of the organization

- Docker containers limit filesystem and process access 

- USB device access is scoped to required Hardware only

- No persistent data is stored inside containers

- system design minimized the attack surface exposed by executing untrusted code

## Ethical Considerations and Mitigations

- Prevent unfair academic advantage by ensuring all student execute code on identical hardware 
- Transparency in grading logic ensures fairness and reproducibility 

- System designed for educational use, not surveillance or student monitoring

## Limitations of the Method

- limited scalability due to reliance on physical hardware availability

- Hardware failures can interrupt CI Workflows

- system currently only supports the Raspberry PI Pico on Linux and Windows Hosts
